title: Audit export integrity: deterministic pagination and role-aware redaction verifier
creator: Aisha Rao
description: Implement an export integrity and verifier pipeline for the Console Audit Viewer that guarantees deterministic pagination order, per-export manifests with cryptographic checksums, and role-aware redaction applied server-side. This ticket covers backend export generation, server-side cursor mechanics for large result sets, UI export controls (CSV / NDJSON), and an automated verifier job that validates exported artifacts and surfaces failure states in the Console and export webhook callbacks.
acceptance_criteria: Exports using server-side cursors produce deterministic ordering across retries when source data is unchanged

Per-export manifest files (.manifest.json) are generated containing: query parameters, timestamp, SHA256 of the payload, total record count, and rbactor-context (masked) — stored alongside exported artifact
RBAC v2 policy evaluation runs at export time and redaction is applied before checksum computation: no sensitive attributes leak into exported files for roles lacking permission
Export formats supported: CSV (column-first, quoted), NDJSON (one JSON object per line). Both formats must preserve stable column ordering for a saved query
Pagination tokens (opaque resume cursor) allow resume of interrupted exports without duplication or omission
Console shows export status (queued, running, verified, failed) and the verifier failure reasons with links to raw manifest and logs
Saved queries retain exact projection and sort-order; re-running a saved query export reproduces identical manifest SHA256 when source data is unchanged
Automated verifier job runs asynchronously after export completion and retries transient failures up to 3x before marking export as failed
Export webhook (enterprise customers) receives a signed callback with manifest metadata and verifier status
Performance: a 100M-row incremental export pipeline can produce a verified NDJSON export within the Dedicated capacity SLOs (validated in load test run)
Unit and integration tests cover: RBAC redaction rules, cursor resume, manifest correctness, checksum validation, and format compatibility with downstream ingestion

reproduction_steps: 1) Create a saved query with multi-column sort and projection that includes potential redactable fields
2) As user with elevated role, trigger an export to NDJSON and wait for verifier completion
3) Immediately mutate underlying audit events (insert and delete) and re-run the saved query export; verify manifest SHA256 remains the same only when run against the same snapshot id
4) As a role with restricted view, attempt the same export and assert redacted columns are absent or masked in downloaded artifact
tech_notes: - Server-side cursor: opaque token encodes snapshot id + last-seen sequence id + sort-order hash
- Deterministic ordering: order by (snapshot_sequence, timestamp, event_id) to avoid non-determinism from concurrent inserts
- Manifest structure: {query, snapshot_id, format, checksum_sha256, record_count, exported_by_role_hash}
- Redaction hook location: immediately after projection stage and before serialization; uses RBAC v2 policy engine (policy evaluation cache keyed by user role + saved-query id)
- Verifier computes SHA256 on the serialized payload stream and compares with manifest; any mismatch marks export as FAILED and surfaces logs
- Storage: artifacts land in customer-segregated buckets for Dedicated/Private; hosted uses per-tenant object namespaces with retention policies
- Telemetry: emit export.performance.* metrics and export.verifier.* events to tracing system and Console timelines
risks: - Large exports may surface race windows between snapshot acquisition and first page; solved by snapshot id but needs performance validation
- RBAC policy changes mid-export could cause inconsistent redaction on resumed exports; mitigation: snapshot policies at start or require policy version pinning
- Increased storage and verifier compute costs for large enterprise exports
- UX confusion if verification fails silently — require explicit UI state and webhook notifications
